newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: India to cut quotas, tariffs on Sri Lanka exports.
newsitem.headline: India to cut quotas, tariffs on Sri Lanka exports.

text.p: India plans to remove quotas and cut tariffs on 70-80 items of Sri Lankan exports, Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Monday.

"(My government has decided) to unilaterally remove quantitative restrictions and reduce tariffs on about 70-80 items of export interest to Sri Lanka," he said in a prepared speech at the start of the third Indo-Lanka Joint Commission meeting.
The changes to India's import policy, to be done within the framework of the South Asian Preferential Trade Agreement (SAPTA), will be announced in April, he said.

Colombo has been trying to get India to remove quantitative restrictions on a variety of items, especially agricultural products like rubber, cloves and cinnamon, and consumer goods like ceramics and confectionery.
The matter figured prominently in talks President Chandrika Kumaratunga held with Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda during her visit to India in December.
Gujral arrived in the island on Sunday on a four-day visit to co-chair the Joint Commission with Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar.
The commission was set up in 1991 to foster bilateral co-operation between the two neighbours. Its last meeting was in April 1994 in New Delhi.

Gujral said a bilateral investment protection agreement the two countries will sign during his visit will give a "new impetus to trade and investment ties and help unleash a new entrepreneurial dynamism".
Colombo has been urging her giant neighbour to import more goods from Sri Lanka and invest more in the island as her balance of trade is now heavily in India's favour.
Kadirgamar said the trade ratio was 1:15 with Sri Lanka's exports to India being $30 million in 1995 and Indian exports to Sri Lanka standing at over $450 million.

"What needs to be done is for India to eliminate both tariff and non-tariff barriers on all commodities and services exported from Sri Lanka with the exception of a small list of sensitive items which India may wish to exclude," he said.
Gujral said he will take up the problem posed by Indian fishermen fishing in Sri Lankan waters separately during talks with Kadirgamar.
Gujral met Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga on Sunday and is scheduled to hold talks with Kadirgamar, Prime Minister Sirima Bandranaike and opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe.
He will also hold talks with leaders of minority Tamil political parties on the Tamil Tiger rebel war for independence in the north and east, now in its 14th year.
